analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date and revises the GLM video description. Head lines 810-813 say variable-frame-rate (VFR) tracks are now indexed rather than refused, with frame i timed at i / nominalFrameRate. Line 829 drops 'including variable-frame-rate video' from the list of deterministic 400 processor refusals. No code is in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify the Swift implementation (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset). Documentation alone changes no security controls.

The documented behavior still keeps the bounds relevant to T-050/TB-007 availability and memory concerns: the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap, the 28,532 visual-token cap, and one-video-at-a-time decode (lines 815, 822-828). The doc also says only the 2 FPS official sample is converted and kept. The source change accepting VFR input broadens the media attack surface, but frame-count and memory bounds are documented as still applying. Whether decode of a VFR track with a misleading nominalFrameRate or very long duration is bounded before RGB conversion, such as a frame-iteration cap, is unverified. The unchanged text does state the decoded-frame cap, which suggests a bound exists.

Other examined text (prefix-cache scope partitioning, SSD cache, the T-041 context) is unchanged. I identified no regression to the T-041 posture (HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL, coordinator-authored scope). The only remaining integration question is whether the matching code change in GLM5NextProcessor enforces frame-count and time bounds for VFR tracks. That code is not supplied in this batch.
